title: AI's Silent Takeover of Service Jobs
caption:
Think AI at the drive-thru is just a quirk? It's a strategic beachhead. McDonald's and Wendy's are piloting systems that hint at a much broader shift in customer service. This isn't just about ordering fries, it's about reshaping the frontline workforce.

Want to understand the next wave of AI integration? BUILD for the field guide.

slides.headline: McDonald's chatbots are just the *start*.
slides.sub: Why your next customer service experience won't be human.

slides.definition: A system designed to interact with humans using natural language, typically via voice or text, to perform tasks or provide information.
slides.example: Taking a drive-thru order or answering common customer queries without human intervention.

stats.label: McDonald's began its AI drive-thru trials.

slides.title: Wendy's and others join in.
bullets: Wendy's partnered with Google Cloud for its "FreshAI" system.
Pilots aim to handle entire order flows, from greeting to payment.
Goal: reduce wait times, improve order accuracy, free up human staff.
slides.footer: This isn't unique to fast food.

audiences.body: Lower labor costs, consistent service quality, faster transaction times, especially during peak hours.
Shorter lines, potentially fewer order errors, and less pressure on human staff leading to better overall interactions.

slides.body: The drive-thru is a proving ground. What starts as a simple order-taker evolves into a sophisticated front-line agent. Expect this integration to accelerate, moving beyond fast food to retail, banking, and beyond. This isn't just about speed; it's about redefining the human role in customer interaction.

slides.sub: Get ahead of the next wave in AI adoption.
